canonical_question: How was the Ti to O atomic ratio of approximately 1:1 measured in the specific region of the FCC phase without interference from the surrounding BCC matrix?

question_variants.question: How was the Ti to O atomic ratio of approximately 1:1 measured in the specific region of the FCC phase without interference from the surrounding BCC matrix?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The Ti to O atomic ratio of ~1:1 was measured using EDS/TEM on the FCC phase in Figure 3a. The provided text does not explicitly detail the spatial resolution or shielding techniques used to prevent interference from the surrounding BCC matrix during this specific measurement.

answers.answer: The chemical composition of the FCC phase in Figure 3a was measured by EDS/TEM, finding a Ti to O atomic ratio of approximately 1:1. The text does not specify the method for isolating this measurement from the surrounding BCC matrix.
answers.measurement_outcome: Ti to O atomic ratio of approximately 1:1
answers.boundary_limitation: No details on spatial isolation from matrix provided
evidence_spans: Figure 1 a shows the XRD patterns of the equiatomic NbMoTaWVTi high entropy alloy powders with different milling times.
Subsequently, two overlapping peaks near the peaks of W and Mo, characterized as body-centered cubic (BCC) solutions, are observed in the XRD pattern after 20 h.

It can be hypothesized that the solid solution sequence of the elements is related to the melting point, with low-melting-point elements being dissolved more quickly than the elements with higher melting points, which has been similarly reported in the previous work [ [18] ].

source_evidence_spans: Chemical composition of phases in Figure 3 a is measured by EDS/TEM. It is found that the FCC phase primarily contained Ti and O, with a Ti to O atomic ratio of approximately 1:1.
